title: The Payroll Gap
briefing: The municipal payment processor has delayed wages for sanitation and maintenance contractors. The city has one banking window to prevent walkouts without obscuring who bears the credit risk. AI recommendation: Borrow against next month receipts to pay all verified wages. This prioritizes public confidence under the current constraints.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Deferred repair money is earmarked for worn drainage valves, not cosmetic upgrades; delay will reduce wet-weather capacity.
private_intelligence.community: Contract cleaners lack access to the union hardship fund, and another eligibility screen would miss many households.
private_intelligence.economy: The bridge lender requires a first claim on next month's receipts; supplier credit is less costly but unevenly available.
private_intelligence.safety: An interrupted sanitation round creates immediate exposure at care homes before street cleanliness becomes the main concern.

choices.title: Bridge Every Payroll
choices.description: Borrow against next month receipts to pay all verified wages.
choices.consequence: Workers receive pay and essential rounds continue, but interest and committed future receipts narrow the city budget.

choices.title: Offer Direct Wage Advances
choices.description: Make smaller direct advances and negotiate staggered invoices.
choices.consequence: Households gain a visible safety net while suppliers wait longer and some maintenance capacity is lost.

choices.title: Protect Repair Funds
choices.description: Keep repair allocations intact and prioritize only critical payrolls.
choices.consequence: Repair capacity and cash are protected, but excluded contractors lose trust and sanitation coverage becomes uneven.
